transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I've just been feeling really down and sad for a very long time now. It has been going on constantly for about two years and two months, and I just can't seem to shake this depressed mood.
You mentioned feeling down for about two years and two months. Have you experienced any periods where your mood significantly improved for at least two months during this time?
No, I don't recall any times where my mood actually improved or felt normal during these past two years. It has just been a constant, heavy cloud without any real breaks.
During this time, have you lost interest in activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy, or have you still been able to find pleasure in the things you normally like to do?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed a complete loss of interest in my hobbies or the things I usually do. It's more just that my mood itself is always so low.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by your mood being 'always so low'? How would you describe the intensity of your sadness, and are there any other symptoms like changes in appetite, sleep, or energy levels that you've noticed?

My sadness feels like a constant, heavy state of emptiness and emotional numbness that has been there continuously for over two years. It doesn't really fluctuate; it's just always present. As for my sleep, appetite, or energy, I haven't noticed any major changes in those areas.

Have you experienced any discrete episodes of depression that lasted for at least two weeks, where you had either depressed mood most of the day or markedly diminished interest or pleasure in activities, along with other symptoms like changes in weight, sleep, or concentration?

I haven't really noticed any separate, distinct episodes or specific changes in my weight or sleep. It has just felt like one long, continuous stretch of low mood and trouble concentrating for the last two years.
How has this constant low mood and trouble concentrating affected your daily life, relationships, and ability to work or go about your usual activities over the past two years?

For the past two years and two months, the lack of concentration and constant cloudiness have made it incredibly hard to focus on my work or make simple daily decisions. I also constantly feel worthless and compare myself negatively to others, which has caused me to withdraw from relationships and feel completely resigned to this state.

Have you ever experienced any unusual perceptions, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others cannot, or held any beliefs that might seem unrealistic or untrue to others, especially in relation to your feelings of worthlessness or low mood?
No, I have never experienced anything like hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there. I also haven't held any unusual or unrealistic beliefs, even when I am feeling my lowest.

Looking back over the past two years, can you think of any two-week period where you experienced at least five symptoms of depression, such as depressed mood, loss of interest, changes in appetite or sleep, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness, or difficulty concentrating?

I'm really not sure, and it is hard to pinpoint any specific two-week period where things were suddenly much worse. These feelings of low mood, worthlessness, and poor concentration have just felt like a constant, steady cloud over the entire two years and two months.
Can you confirm that your low mood has been present for most of the day, more days than not, for at least two years, which is the majority of the time since it started?
Yes, that's exactly how it is. My low mood has been there almost every single day, for most of the day, for the entire two years and two months. It really hasn't let up at all during this whole time.

It sounds like you've been experiencing a persistent low mood for an extended period. I'd like to summarize: you've had a depressed mood for most of the day, more days than not, for at least two years, with feelings of worthlessness and poor concentration, but without any distinct episodes of major depression or psychotic symptoms. Is that a correct summary of your experience?

Yes, that is a completely accurate summary of my experience. This constant low mood, worthlessness, and trouble focusing have indeed been dragging on for two years and two months now, without any sudden spikes or unusual experiences.
